said:
Reckoning the years
People use the Belt Standard Calendar, introduced with the Charter that connected the first settlements of the Lantern Belt.
The era is called Charter Reckoning, abbreviated CR. The story begins on 18 Rainfall, 186 CR, early in the local autumn on Nacre.
This calendar is a human convention. The seasons below apply to the Vesper Coast on Nacre; other planets follow their own climates. Stations and ships keep the same standard time for duty rosters, appointments and logs.
Months
Twelve months have thirty days each. The thirteenth consists of five closing days: together, 365 days per year.
| # | Month | Days | Season on the Vesper Coast |
| 1 | Deepnight | 30 | Winter |
| 2 | Frostline | 30 | Winter |
| 3 | Thaw | 30 | Spring |
| 4 | Runoff | 30 | Spring |
| 5 | Firstlight | 30 | Spring |
| 6 | Longday | 30 | Summer |
| 7 | Highsun | 30 | Summer |
| 8 | Stillwater | 30 | Summer |
| 9 | Rainfall | 30 | Autumn — starting month |
| 10 | Greywind | 30 | Autumn |
| 11 | Lastlight | 30 | Autumn |
| 12 | Longdark | 30 | Winter |
| 13 | Intercalary | 5 | Winter; year-end |

The names come from early colonisation. On space stations, Highsun and Rainfall signify only a date.
The five days of Intercalary are used for maintenance, stocktaking, remembrance and closing out contracts. Ordinary work continues where necessary.
Week
A week has five days:
1.  Primeday
2.  Span
3.  Relay
4.  Anchor
5.  Restday
The week continues normally during Intercalary. Restday is traditionally a day of rest, but port staff, medical services and life support operate in shifts.
Weather on Nacre
The Vesper Coast lies in a cold, windy coastal zone. The outside air is breathable, but cold, sea spray and prolonged exposure make protective clothing important.
| Season | Weather | Meaning for play |
| Spring | Cold rain, meltwater, low mist and sudden clear spells. | Low routes may flood; maintenance teams repair winter damage. |
| Summer | Cool, long daylight hours, sea mist and some clear periods. | The best season for outdoor work and transport; clear visibility reveals distant landmarks. |
| Autumn | Persistent rain, strong winds, heavy seas and storm fronts. | Landings may be delayed; the road to Orison Ridge becomes more dangerous and antennas are damaged. |
| Winter | Wet snow, freezing rain, hail and long dark periods. | Outdoor work requires preparation; ice can block doors, vehicles and emergency exits. |

Weather at the start
On arrival, light, steady rain is falling. The wind comes from the sea, and the top of Orison Ridge frequently disappears into the clouds. A storm front is expected within two days: a forecast with uncertainty, not a guaranteed disaster.
Indoors and aboard ship
No local weather is simulated inside enclosed buildings or aboard the Peregrine. Outside weather remains noticeable only where it makes sense: rain against a window, vibrations during a storm, delayed supplies or someone arriving soaked through.
In space, malfunctions, radiation and anomalous sensor readings are separate events with a cause. Do not use them as random “space weather”. Echo Nine’s climate is established during worldbuilding, but remains unknown to the player until reliable measurements become available.
For the Chronicler: let weather primarily affect routes, visibility, work and appointments. Mention it again when it changes or matters; do not repeat that it is raining with every action.
